clue.text: Black man discarded material on beach

parts.note: jet is a deep black stone, so jet-black means black
Sam is a man's name

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned beachcomber is accused of leaving rubbish on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard that washes up on the shore, the classic flotsam's companion.

clue.text: Book Two going out in large numbers

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Bible, after Genesis

explanation.definitionFit: Exodus is both the second Old Testament book and a general word for a mass departure.

clue.text: He caps Mitty's version, showing affinity of feeling

indicators.note: a version is a rendering in another form, so these letters are given in a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone's take on Walter Mitty, crowned by another man, reveals a fellow-feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges HE, CAPS and MITTY (the possessive 's adds no letter). Walter Mitty is the daydreaming hero of James Thurber's story.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sympathetic is to share or show feeling for another, an affinity of emotion.

clue.text: Married woman, member of large family, serving as model

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name
a quin is one of five babies born together, quintuplets

explanation.surface: A wife from a family of quintuplets works as a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving as' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannequin is a dummy or person used to display clothes, i.e. a model.

clue.text: Porter's rules for making salad?

parts.note: Cole Porter, the American songwriter, so Porter's gives Cole's
law is a body of rules

explanation.surface: A songwriter's recipe guide for preparing a salad, with a playful question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rule book; read it as 'Cole's law', the songwriter's name plus a word for rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage in dressing.

clue.text: City set down in mathematical shape

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the record sitting within the shape

parts.note: a cone is a solid geometric shape
to log is to record or write down

explanation.surface: A town is laid out in the form of a geometric figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a large German city on the Rhine, an instance of the definition.

clue.text: First woman in Lord Lieutenant's flat

indicators.note: the first woman's name goes inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for Lord
L is an abbreviation for Lieutenant
in Genesis Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: The first woman is living in a nobleman's apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Level means flat or even, as a level surface.

clue.text: A shining example of popular journalism!

definitions.meaning: our star, which shines over us
the name of a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: The star at the centre of the solar system shines; it is also a famous British tabloid title.

clue.text: Like mauve and taupe spades carried by a boy soldier

indicators.note: the card suit's letter is held within the following pieces

parts.note: a son is a boy
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
a soldier ant is a worker that defends the colony; ant is a common crossword soldier

explanation.surface: Two drab colours of a card suit are borne by a young army recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Mauve and taupe share their vowel sounds without rhyming fully, which is assonance.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonant describes words that echo each other's vowel sounds, as mauve and taupe do.

clue.text: Shared fuel, accommodating many retired miners

indicators.note: the fuel takes in the other pieces, as a host accommodates guests

parts.note: coal is a fuel
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, i.e. many

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the union's letters run backwards

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

explanation.surface: Fuel is pooled to house a large number of former pit workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Communal means shared by a community or group.

clue.text: Conquer, without question, but mysteriously disappear

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the question's letters come out of the conquering word

parts.note: to vanquish is to conquer

explanation.surface: Win without a doubt, then strangely vanish from sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to disappear suddenly, often without explanation.

clue.text: Short note welcoming a junior cleric

indicators.note: the outer pieces take in the article as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: curt means short or abrupt
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A brief message greets a newly arrived young clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant clergyman, junior to the vicar or rector.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise about language that's used in films

indicators.note: the exclamation goes round the language, about meaning surrounding

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
Latin is a language

explanation.surface: Someone gasps over a language spoken in the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatine is the binding layer that holds light-sensitive chemicals on photographic film.

clue.text: Newspaper moving fast to attain optimum use of computer

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper
haring means running fast like a hare

explanation.surface: A newspaper is rushing to make the best use of its computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to attain' just links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-sharing lets many users use one computer at once, making maximal use of its processing time.

clue.text: Party from legislature preparing for conflict with West

parts.note: a House, such as the House of Commons, is a legislative chamber
arming means getting weapons ready for war

explanation.surface: A political party from parliament is gearing up for war alongside the West.
explanation.definitionFit: A housewarming is a party held to celebrate moving into a new home.

clue.text: Rich area making dynamic progress

parts.note: bounding means advancing in leaps

explanation.surface: A wealthy region is advancing by leaps and bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Abounding means plentiful, rich in something, as in a land abounding in fish.

clue.text: Packet accommodating posters overseas?

parts.note: a packet is also a ship on a regular route; here it carries what people have posted to other countries

explanation.surface: A parcel with room for overseas posters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packet' looks like a parcel but is a packet boat, a vessel carrying letters; 'posters' are people who post them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail-boat is a ship carrying post, formerly called a packet or packet boat.

clue.text: Irascible old American stuck behind prison vehicle

indicators.note: the last two pieces are placed after the prison and vehicle

parts.note: can is slang for prison
a tanker is a vehicle carrying liquid

explanation.surface: A grumpy elderly Yank is trapped behind a prison truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous means bad-tempered and quarrelsome, a close synonym of irascible.

clue.text: Disclosure of European casual about bribe set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the letters read upward, i.e. backwards
the casual word goes round the bribe

parts.note: lax means casual or slack
a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe

explanation.surface: A relaxed European is caught out in a rigged bribery scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' suits a down clue: the bribe-in-casual combination, LASOPX, is read from the bottom, giving XPOSAL after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposal is an uncommon word for exposure, revealing something hidden.

clue.text: Seaman is prone to climb and descend by rope

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upward, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: lies means is lying down, prone

explanation.surface: A sailor is inclined to go up and come down on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a rock face or building using a rope.

clue.text: Bird once assumed to herald death?

definitions.meaning: a small warbler with a dark crown
a British judge formerly put on a black head covering before passing a death sentence

explanation.definitionFit: It names a warbler and the black head covering a judge put on to pronounce a death sentence.

clue.text: Like sugar lumps a youngster imprudently consumes for starters

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or Cub Scout

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: A child foolishly eats sugar lumps as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar lumps are cubes, so they are cubic in shape.

clue.text: Supporter in desire to return somewhere close

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the combined letters read backwards
the supporter goes inside the desire

parts.note: a yen is a longing
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A fan wants to go back somewhere close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' is a garment here, not a fan; the container YBRAEN is read backwards for 'to return'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means at a short distance, somewhere close.

clue.text: No end of pleasant activity, inviting small number in to socialise

indicators.note: the trimmed pastime takes in the number, as a host invites a guest in
the last letter of the pastime is dropped

parts.note: a hobby is an enjoyable pastime
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Endless fun, with a few people invited along to mingle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'endless', but it means the pastime loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, especially with important people.

clue.text: Tipster's choice to take forty winks

definitions.meaning: a racing tipster's most confident selection

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a horse-racing tipster's best bet and a doze.

clue.text: Lively game

definitions.meaning: willing and brave, as in game for anything

explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means energetic and also plucky, ready to have a go.

clue.text: A person out East I mostly consider unrepresentative

indicators.note: the compass letter is put out of the word for a person

parts.note: a type can mean a person, as in an odd type

indicators.note: most of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: to call can mean to judge or consider

explanation.surface: Someone from the Orient is, I think, not typical.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, unrepresentative of its kind.

clue.text: See soldier taking turn to be first escort

indicators.note: the soldier and turn come before the word for see

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a go is a turn
lo is an old word for look or see

explanation.surface: Watch a soldier taking his turn to lead the escort.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to escort a woman.
